title: Ninth Circuit vacates injunction against Perplexity's Comet agent, holding the user, not the vendor, accessed Amazon
summary: In a 3-0 decision reported on 6 August 2026, a Ninth Circuit panel (Judge Milan Smith Jr. writing, with Judges Eric Tung and John Hinderaker) vacated the preliminary injunction that Judge Maxine Chesney had issued in March against Perplexity AI's Comet browser, which can compare products and complete purchases on Amazon.com on a user's behalf and which the order had also required to delete copies of Amazon data; the panel found the district court abused its discretion in holding Amazon likely to win under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act and California's related statute, because it is the user, assisted by Comet, who accesses Amazon's computers, and Amazon's reading could expose users themselves to criminal liability. The panel said the decision is confined to CFAA access on this record and does not "establish a new legal regime governing agentic AI"; the case returns to the district court with the underlying dispute undecided, and Amazon says it disagrees with the ruling and is evaluating its next steps.
